question: 彼{かれ}は十年{じゅうねん}もアメリカに住{す}んでいた（　　）、英語{えいご}の発音{はつおん}がとてもきれいだ。
full_sentence: 彼{かれ}は十年{じゅうねん}もアメリカに住{す}んでいただけあって、英語{えいご}の発音{はつおん}がとてもきれいだ。
translation: As you would expect from someone who lived in America for ten years, his English pronunciation is very beautiful.
explanation: The first half gives a cause (he lived in America for as long as ten years) and the second half gives the result you would naturally expect from that cause (his pronunciation is beautiful). 〜だけあって means 'as you would expect from ~, precisely because ~' and is used to praise a result that matches the cause, someone's effort, or their status. The particle も in 十年も 'as many as ten years' stresses how long the stay was, which strengthens the 'no wonder!' feeling. Connection: plain form of verbs and い-adjectives (住んでいた, 高い), な-adjective + な (有名な), or a noun directly (プロだけあって). The other three choices all express some kind of contrast ('considering', 'even though', 'although'), but in this sentence there is no contrast: the cause and the result point in the same direction.
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜わりに means 'considering ~, for ~' and introduces a result that is DIFFERENT from what you would expect (年のわりに若く見える 'he looks young for his age'). Ten years in America makes you expect good pronunciation, and the result is good pronunciation, so nothing is unexpected. Correct use: 十年もアメリカに住んでいたわりに、英語が下手だ 'for someone who lived in America for ten years, his English is poor'.

Wrong. 〜くせに means 'even though ~' with criticism or contempt. It needs a contrast plus a negative feeling: 十年もアメリカに住んでいたくせに、英語が全然話せない 'even though he lived in America for ten years, he can't speak English at all (how annoying)'. Our sentence is praise, so くせに does not fit.

Correct. 住んでいただけあって 'just as you would expect from having lived there (for ten years)'. The cause (a long stay) and the praiseworthy result (beautiful pronunciation) match. Connection: plain form + だけあって.

Wrong. 〜ものの means 'although ~' and introduces a contrast: the second half goes against what the first half suggests. Correct use: 十年もアメリカに住んでいたものの、英語はあまり上手にならなかった 'although he lived in America for ten years, his English didn't get very good'. Our sentence has no contrast.

vocab.example: この単語{たんご}の発音{はつおん}は難{むずか}しい。
vocab.example_translation: The pronunciation of this word is difficult.

vocab.meaning: to live (in a place), to reside
vocab.example: 私{わたし}は東京{とうきょう}に住{す}んでいる。
vocab.example_translation: I live in Tokyo.

vocab.meaning: as many as, as long as (emphasizes that a number is large)
vocab.example: 駅{えき}まで一時間{いちじかん}も歩{ある}いた。
vocab.example_translation: I walked for as long as an hour to the station.

grammar.meaning: as you would expect from ~, precisely because ~ (the result matches the cause; usually praise)
grammar.formation: Plain form (verb / い-adj) / な-adj + な / noun + だけあって
grammar.example: さすがプロの選手{せんしゅ}だけあって、動{うご}きが速{はや}い。
grammar.example_translation: As you would expect from a professional athlete, his movements are fast.

grammar.meaning: considering ~, for ~ (the result differs from what you would expect)
grammar.formation: Plain form / な-adj + な / noun + の + わりに
grammar.example: 彼{かれ}は年{とし}のわりに若{わか}く見{み}える。
grammar.example_translation: He looks young for his age.

grammar.meaning: even though ~ (with criticism, contempt, or annoyance)
grammar.formation: Plain form / な-adj + な / noun + の + くせに (same subject in both halves)
grammar.example: 弟{おとうと}は自分{じぶん}ではできないくせに、文句{もんく}ばかり言{い}う。
grammar.example_translation: My younger brother complains all the time even though he can't do it himself.

grammar.meaning: although ~ (it is true, but the result is not what the first half suggests)
grammar.formation: Plain form / な-adj + な (or である) / noun + である + ものの
grammar.example: 新{あたら}しいパソコンを買{か}ったものの、使{つか}い方{かた}がよくわからない。
grammar.example_translation: Although I bought a new computer, I don't really know how to use it.

question: 駅{えき}の忘{わす}れ物{もの}センターに電話{でんわ}で問{と}い合{あ}わせ（　　）、なくした財布{さいふ}が届{とど}いていることがわかった。
full_sentence: 駅{えき}の忘{わす}れ物{もの}センターに電話{でんわ}で問{と}い合{あ}わせたところ、なくした財布{さいふ}が届{とど}いていることがわかった。
translation: When I phoned the station's lost-and-found center to ask, I found out that the wallet I had lost had been handed in.
explanation: 〜たところ means 'when I did ~, (it turned out that) ~'. The first half is an action the speaker did (phoning to ask), and the second half is the result or discovery that came from it (the wallet had been handed in). The ending 〜ことがわかった 'it became clear that ~' is a strong clue, because たところ is very often followed by a discovery. The result can be good or bad, and it is usually something outside the speaker's control (so you don't put your own intention after it). Connection: verb た-form + ところ. 問い合わせる is an ichidan verb, so its た-form is 問い合わせた; that is why every choice begins with た.
choice_notes: Correct. 問い合わせたところ 'when I inquired, (it turned out that) ~'. An action followed by a discovered result. Connection: た-form + ところ.

Wrong. 〜たばかりに means 'just because ~ (a bad result happened)' and expresses regret. Our result (the wallet was found) is good news, so it does not fit. Correct use: 財布を後ろのポケットに入れたばかりに、すられてしまった 'just because I put my wallet in my back pocket, it got pickpocketed'.

Wrong. 〜たあげく means 'after a lot of ~, in the end ~' and needs a long, tiring process, usually with a negative result. One phone call is not a long struggle. Correct use: さんざん迷ったあげく、何も買わなかった 'after agonizing over it for ages, I ended up buying nothing'.

Wrong. 〜たきり means 'did ~ and then nothing since' (the expected next thing never happened) and is usually followed by a negative: 彼は朝出かけたきり、まだ帰ってこない 'he went out in the morning and still hasn't come back'. It does not introduce a discovery.

vocab.example: 電車{でんしゃ}に忘{わす}れ物{もの}をしてしまった。
vocab.example_translation: I left something behind on the train.

vocab.meaning: to inquire, to make an inquiry
vocab.example: 予約{よやく}について、ホテルに問{と}い合{あ}わせた。
vocab.example_translation: I inquired at the hotel about my reservation.

vocab.example: 財布{さいふ}を家{いえ}に忘{わす}れてきた。
vocab.example_translation: I left my wallet at home.

vocab.meaning: to arrive, to be delivered; (of a lost item) to be handed in
vocab.example: 昨日{きのう}注文{ちゅうもん}した本{ほん}がもう届{とど}いた。
vocab.example_translation: The book I ordered yesterday has already arrived.

vocab.example: 大切{たいせつ}な鍵{かぎ}をなくしてしまった。
vocab.example_translation: I lost an important key.

grammar.meaning: when I did ~, (it turned out that) ~; I did ~ and found that ~
grammar.formation: Verb た-form + ところ
grammar.example: 先生{せんせい}に相談{そうだん}したところ、いいアドバイスをもらえた。
grammar.example_translation: When I consulted my teacher, I got some good advice.

grammar.meaning: just because ~, simply because ~ (a bad result followed; regret)
grammar.formation: Plain form (often た-form) / な-adj + な / noun + である + ばかりに
grammar.example: 寝坊{ねぼう}したばかりに、大事{だいじ}な試験{しけん}に遅{おく}れた。
grammar.example_translation: Just because I overslept, I was late for an important exam.

grammar.meaning: after a lot of ~, in the end ~ (usually a negative or tiring result)
grammar.formation: Verb た-form / noun + の + あげく
grammar.example: 長{なが}い時間{じかん}話{はな}し合{あ}ったあげく、結論{けつろん}は出{で}なかった。
grammar.example_translation: After discussing it for a long time, in the end no conclusion was reached.

grammar.meaning: did ~ and then nothing since (the expected next thing hasn't happened)
grammar.formation: Verb た-form + きり (often followed by a negative)
grammar.example: 兄{あに}とは五年前{ごねんまえ}に会{あ}ったきりだ。
grammar.example_translation: I haven't seen my older brother since I met him five years ago.

question: 部屋{へや}のドアを開{あ}けた（　　）、猫{ねこ}が外{そと}へ飛{と}び出{だ}していった。
full_sentence: 部屋{へや}のドアを開{あ}けたとたん、猫{ねこ}が外{そと}へ飛{と}び出{だ}していった。
translation: The moment I opened the door of the room, the cat dashed outside.
explanation: 〜たとたん(に) means 'the instant ~, just as ~' and describes something that happens immediately after the first action, usually unexpectedly. Opening the door, and at that very moment the cat dashed out: this surprise and speed is exactly the nuance of とたん. Connection: verb た-form + とたん(に). Note that the second half must be something that actually happened (a fact), and it is usually outside the speaker's control. You cannot put your own intention, a request, or an order after とたん (×ドアを開けたとたん、外に出よう).
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜うちに means 'while ~ (before the situation changes)' and connects to a continuing state, not to a completed た-form: 若いうちに, 熱いうちに, 雨が降らないうちに. 開けたうちに is ungrammatical. Correct use: 熱いうちに食べてください 'please eat it while it's hot'.

Wrong. 〜あいだに means 'during ~, while ~' and needs a period of time, so it attaches to a ている-form or noun + の, not to a completed action: 私が寝ているあいだに、泥棒が入った 'while I was sleeping, a thief broke in'. 開けたあいだに is ungrammatical.

Wrong. 〜以上（いじょう）(は) means 'now that ~, since ~' and is followed by a duty, a resolution, or a strong judgment: 約束した以上、守らなければならない 'now that I've promised, I must keep it'. A cat running out is not a duty or a judgment, so it does not fit.
Correct. 開けたとたん 'the moment I opened it'. An action followed by an immediate, unexpected event. Connection: た-form + とたん.

vocab.meaning: to rush out, to jump out, to dash out
vocab.example: 子{こ}どもが急{きゅう}に道{みち}に飛{と}び出{だ}してきた。
vocab.example_translation: A child suddenly ran out into the road.

vocab.meaning: to do ~ and go (movement away from the speaker)
vocab.example: 鳥{とり}が空{そら}へ飛{と}んでいった。
vocab.example_translation: The bird flew away into the sky.

vocab.example: 暑{あつ}いので窓{まど}を開{あ}けてください。
vocab.example_translation: It's hot, so please open the window.

grammar.meaning: the moment ~, just as ~ (something unexpected happened right after)
grammar.formation: Verb た-form + とたん(に)
grammar.example: 立{た}ち上{あ}がったとたん、頭{あたま}が痛{いた}くなった。
grammar.example_translation: The moment I stood up, my head started to hurt.

grammar.meaning: while ~ (do it before the situation changes)
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary / ている / ない-form, い-adj, な-adj + な, noun + の + うちに
grammar.example: 忘{わす}れないうちに、メモしておこう。
grammar.example_translation: Let's write it down before I forget.

grammar.meaning: while ~, during ~ (something happens at some point within the period)
grammar.formation: Verb ている-form / noun + の + あいだに
grammar.example: 母{はは}が買{か}い物{もの}をしているあいだに、部屋{へや}を掃除{そうじ}した。
grammar.example_translation: While my mother was out shopping, I cleaned the room.

grammar.meaning: now that ~, since ~ (so one must / naturally ~)
grammar.formation: Plain form / noun + である + 以上(は)
grammar.example: 引{ひ}き受{う}けた以上{いじょう}、最後{さいご}まで責任{せきにん}を持{も}つべきだ。
grammar.example_translation: Now that you've taken it on, you should be responsible for it until the end.

question: こんなにたくさんの宿題{しゅくだい}、一晩{ひとばん}でなんか（　　）よ。
choices: 終{お}わるに決{き}まっている
full_sentence: こんなにたくさんの宿題{しゅくだい}、一晩{ひとばん}でなんか終{お}わりっこないよ。
translation: There's no way I can finish this much homework in a single night.
explanation: 〜っこない is a casual, spoken way to say 'there's no way ~, ~ is impossible'. It is the conversational version of 〜わけがない / 〜はずがない. The clues are こんなにたくさん 'this much' and 〜なんか, which the speaker uses to dismiss something as unrealistic ('in one night? no way'). The sentence-final よ also fits casual speech. Connection: verb ます-stem + っこない (終わります → 終わり + っこない). It is used mostly with potential or ability verbs such as できる (できっこない), わかる (わかりっこない) and 勝てる (勝てっこない), but it also works with other verbs like 終わる when the meaning is 'it can't possibly happen' (終わりっこない 'it can't possibly get finished'). Because two choices look almost the same, this question also tests the connection rule.
choice_notes: Wrong. This is a connection error. っこない attaches to the ます-stem, not to the dictionary form: 終わる → 終わり + っこない. 終わるっこない does not exist. Compare: できっこない, わかりっこない.
Correct. 終わりっこない 'it can't possibly be finished'. ます-stem 終わり + っこない. A casual, strong denial of possibility.

Wrong. 〜かねない means 'might (unfortunately) ~' and is only used for outcomes the speaker sees as BAD or dangerous: このままでは事故を起こしかねない 'at this rate, he could cause an accident'. Finishing homework is a good thing, and the speaker is denying that it is possible, not warning about it.

Wrong. 〜に決まっている means 'it's sure to ~, of course ~'. 終わるに決まっている 'it will definitely be finished' is the opposite of what the speaker means: こんなにたくさん and なんか show they think it's impossible. Correct use: 彼が来るに決まっている 'of course he'll come'.

vocab.example: 一晩{ひとばん}寝{ね}たら、熱{ねつ}が下{さ}がった。
vocab.example_translation: After sleeping one night, my fever went down.

vocab.meaning: things like ~, the likes of ~ (dismissive or belittling)
vocab.example: 私{わたし}なんか、まだまだ下手{へた}です。
vocab.example_translation: Someone like me is still far from good.

vocab.meaning: this much, so (much), to this extent
vocab.example: こんなにおいしいケーキは初{はじ}めて食{た}べた。
vocab.example_translation: This is the first time I've eaten such a delicious cake.

vocab.example: 宿題{しゅくだい}を忘{わす}れて、先生{せんせい}に注意{ちゅうい}された。
vocab.example_translation: I forgot my homework and was warned by the teacher.

grammar.meaning: there's no way ~, can't possibly ~ (casual speech)
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + っこない
grammar.example: そんな難{むずか}しい問題{もんだい}、子{こ}どもにわかりっこない。
grammar.example_translation: There's no way a child could understand such a difficult problem.

grammar.meaning: might ~, could (possibly) ~ (a bad outcome)
grammar.formation: Verb ます-stem + かねない
grammar.example: そんな運転{うんてん}をしていたら、事故{じこ}を起{お}こしかねない。
grammar.example_translation: If you drive like that, you could end up causing an accident.

grammar.meaning: it's certain that ~, of course ~ (the speaker's strong conviction)
grammar.formation: Plain form / な-adj stem / noun + に決まっている
grammar.example: 毎日{まいにち}遊{あそ}んでばかりいたら、試験{しけん}に落{お}ちるに決{き}まっている。
grammar.example_translation: If you do nothing but play every day, you're bound to fail the exam.

question: 三年前{さんねんまえ}に日本{にほん}に来{き}て（　　）、一度{いちど}も国{くに}に帰{かえ}っていない。
full_sentence: 三年前{さんねんまえ}に日本{にほん}に来{き}て以来{いらい}、一度{いちど}も国{くに}に帰{かえ}っていない。
translation: Since coming to Japan three years ago, I haven't gone back to my home country even once.
explanation: 〜て以来 means 'ever since ~' and describes a state that has continued from one point in the past until now. The second half 一度も帰っていない 'I haven't gone back even once (up to now)' uses 〜ていない to show a continuing state, which is the typical partner of て以来. 三年前に marks the single past point where the state started. Connection: verb て-form + 以来, or noun + 以来 (卒業以来 'since graduation'). It is a little more formal than 〜てから, and it is usually not used for very recent events (×昨日来て以来).
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜てからでないと means 'not until ~, unless ~ first' and is followed by something impossible or not allowed: 手を洗ってからでないと、食べてはいけない 'you can't eat until you've washed your hands'. It states a necessary condition, not the time that has passed since an event.

Wrong. 〜てはじめて means 'only after ~ (did I realize / become able to)' and is followed by a new realization or a first-time experience: 日本に来てはじめて、雪を見た 'only after coming to Japan did I see snow'. It cannot describe a continuing state like 一度も帰っていない.
Correct. 来て以来 'ever since I came'. て-form + 以来, followed by a state that continues up to now.

Wrong. 〜ているうちに means 'while ~ (something changed, often without my noticing)': 日本に住んでいるうちに、納豆が好きになった 'while living in Japan, I came to like natto'. It describes an ongoing period and needs a change in the second half, so it clashes with 三年前に (one point in time) and with 一度も帰っていない (no change).

vocab.example: 夏休{なつやす}みに国{くに}へ帰{かえ}ります。
vocab.example_translation: I'll go back to my home country for the summer vacation.

vocab.example: 富士山{ふじさん}には一度{いちど}も登{のぼ}ったことがない。
vocab.example_translation: I have never climbed Mt. Fuji, not even once.

vocab.meaning: three years ago (number + 年前 = '~ years ago')
vocab.example: 三年前{さんねんまえ}にこの町{まち}に引{ひ}っ越{こ}してきた。
vocab.example_translation: I moved to this town three years ago.

grammar.meaning: ever since ~ (a state continuing from then until now)
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + 以来 / noun + 以来
grammar.example: 大学{だいがく}を卒業{そつぎょう}して以来{いらい}、彼{かれ}には会{あ}っていない。
grammar.example_translation: I haven't seen him since we graduated from university.

grammar.meaning: not until ~, unless ~ first (followed by 'can't' or a difficult result)
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + からでないと / からでなければ
grammar.example: 部長{ぶちょう}に確認{かくにん}してからでないと、お返事{へんじ}できません。
grammar.example_translation: I can't give you an answer until I've checked with the department manager.

grammar.meaning: only after ~ (did one realize / become able to)
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + はじめて
grammar.example: 病気{びょうき}になってはじめて、健康{けんこう}の大切{たいせつ}さがわかった。
grammar.example_translation: Only after getting sick did I understand how important health is.

grammar.meaning: while ~ (a change happened during that time, often unnoticed)
grammar.formation: Verb ている-form + うちに
grammar.example: 本{ほん}を読{よ}んでいるうちに、眠{ねむ}くなった。
grammar.example_translation: While I was reading a book, I got sleepy.

question: この中級{ちゅうきゅう}コースは、初級{しょきゅう}クラスを修了{しゅうりょう}して（　　）、申{もう}し込{こ}むことができない。
full_sentence: この中級{ちゅうきゅう}コースは、初級{しょきゅう}クラスを修了{しゅうりょう}してからでないと、申{もう}し込{こ}むことができない。
translation: You can't apply for this intermediate course until you have completed the beginner class.
explanation: 〜てからでないと means 'not until ~, unless ~ is done first' and is followed by a negative or 'impossible' result (できない, 無理だ, わからない). The sentence ends with 申し込むことができない 'cannot apply', and that negative ending is the big clue: completing the beginner class is a necessary condition that must come first. You can understand the form piece by piece: て-form + から 'after' + でないと 'if it is not', so 'if it is not after completing it, you can't apply'. Connection: verb て-form + からでないと (also からでなければ). Two of the wrong choices (はじめて and こそ) also mean 'only after / only by', but they need a POSITIVE ending.
choice_notes: Correct. 修了してからでないと…できない 'you can't ~ unless you've completed it first'. て-form + からでないと + negative result.

Wrong. 〜て以来 means 'ever since ~' and describes a state continuing from a past event: 修了して以来、一度も勉強していない 'I haven't studied once since I completed it'. It cannot express a rule about what you need to do first.

Wrong, but close. 〜てはじめて means 'only after ~' and is followed by a POSITIVE result or a new realization: 初級クラスを修了してはじめて、申し込むことができる 'only after completing the beginner class can you apply'. Our sentence ends with the negative できない, which needs からでないと.

Wrong. 〜てこそ means 'only by (actually) doing ~ (does something good happen)' and is followed by a positive evaluation: 自分でやってこそ、本当の力がつく 'only by doing it yourself do you gain real skill'. It does not combine with a negative rule like 申し込むことができない.

vocab.example: 中級{ちゅうきゅう}の教科書{きょうかしょ}は少{すこ}し難{むずか}しい。
vocab.example_translation: The intermediate textbook is a little difficult.

vocab.example: 初級{しょきゅう}クラスで日本語{にほんご}を勉強{べんきょう}している。
vocab.example_translation: I'm studying Japanese in a beginner class.

vocab.example: 研修{けんしゅう}を修了{しゅうりょう}すると、証明書{しょうめいしょ}がもらえる。
vocab.example_translation: When you complete the training, you receive a certificate.

vocab.meaning: to apply for, to sign up for
vocab.example: 来月{らいげつ}のマラソン大会{たいかい}に申{もう}し込{こ}んだ。
vocab.example_translation: I signed up for next month's marathon.

grammar.meaning: not until ~, unless ~ first (followed by 'can't' or a difficult result)
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + からでないと / からでなければ
grammar.example: 部長{ぶちょう}に確認{かくにん}してからでないと、お返事{へんじ}できません。
grammar.example_translation: I can't give you an answer until I've checked with the department manager.

grammar.meaning: ever since ~ (a state continuing from then until now)
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + 以来 / noun + 以来
grammar.example: 大学{だいがく}を卒業{そつぎょう}して以来{いらい}、彼{かれ}には会{あ}っていない。
grammar.example_translation: I haven't seen him since we graduated from university.

grammar.meaning: only after ~ (did one realize / become able to)
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + はじめて
grammar.example: 病気{びょうき}になってはじめて、健康{けんこう}の大切{たいせつ}さがわかった。
grammar.example_translation: Only after getting sick did I understand how important health is.

grammar.meaning: only by (actually) doing ~ (is something good or real achieved)
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + こそ

question: 一人{ひとり}で暮{く}らしている母{はは}の体{からだ}のことが、心配{しんぱい}で（　　）。
full_sentence: 一人{ひとり}で暮{く}らしている母{はは}の体{からだ}のことが、心配{しんぱい}でならない。
translation: I'm terribly worried about the health of my mother, who lives alone.
explanation: 〜てならない means 'I can't help feeling ~, I feel ~ terribly' and expresses a strong feeling that rises naturally and can't be controlled. It is used with words of emotion or sensation such as 心配だ 'worried', 不安だ 'anxious', 残念だ 'disappointed', 気になる 'bothered', and 思われる 'it seems'. Here the speaker can't stop worrying about her mother's health. Connection: verb or い-adjective て-form + ならない; な-adjectives use で: 心配で + ならない. Do not confuse it with 〜てはならない 'must not': the single particle は completely changes the meaning. Similar patterns: 心配でたまらない and the more casual 心配でしょうがない.
choice_notes: Wrong (the classic trap). 〜てはならない means 'must not ~' (a formal prohibition): 人の物を盗んではならない 'you must not steal other people's things'. 心配ではならない would mean 'you must not be worried', which does not describe the speaker's feeling. The extra は changes everything.

Wrong. 〜てもかまわない means 'it's all right even if ~, I don't mind if ~': 少し遅れてもかまわない 'it's fine even if you're a little late'. 'It's all right to be worried about my mother's health' does not fit; the sentence expresses a strong feeling, not permission.
Wrong. This is a connection error. 〜てほしい 'I want (someone) to ~' attaches to a VERB て-form: 母にはいつまでも元気でいてほしい 'I want my mother to stay healthy forever'. 心配でほしい is ungrammatical.
Correct. 心配でならない 'I can't help worrying, I'm terribly worried'. な-adjective + で + ならない for an uncontrollable feeling.

question: 今日{きょう}は暖{あたた}かい（　　）、むしろ暑{あつ}いくらいだ。
full_sentence: 今日{きょう}は暖{あたた}かいというより、むしろ暑{あつ}いくらいだ。
translation: Today it's not so much warm as almost hot.
explanation: 〜というより means 'rather than (calling it) ~, it's more like ~'. You first give one description (warm) and then correct it with a more accurate one (hot). The adverb むしろ 'rather, if anything' is the strongest clue, because 〜というより、むしろ〜 is a fixed combination. 〜くらいだ 'to the extent of ~, almost ~' adds that it is close to being hot. Connection: plain form of verbs and い-adjectives, or a noun / な-adjective stem + というより (だ is usually dropped: 静かというより, 先生というより).
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜といっても means 'although I say ~, (it's not as much as you'd think)' and is followed by a LIMITATION: 暖かいといっても、まだコートは必要だ 'it may be warm, but you still need a coat'. むしろ暑い goes beyond 'warm' instead of limiting it, so といっても does not fit.
Correct. 暖かいというより、むしろ暑い 'not so much warm as hot'. Plain form + というより, often followed by むしろ.
Wrong. 〜というと means 'speaking of ~, when you say ~' and introduces a topic or what comes to mind: 京都というと、お寺を思い出す 'speaking of Kyoto, I think of temples'. It does not compare two descriptions.
Wrong. 〜わりには means 'considering ~, for ~' and introduces a result that differs from expectation: 三月のわりには暖かい 'it's warm for March'. 'For being warm, it's rather hot' makes no sense.

vocab.meaning: rather, if anything, on the contrary
vocab.example: 失敗{しっぱい}は悪{わる}いことではなく、むしろいい経験{けいけん}だ。
vocab.example_translation: Failure isn't a bad thing; if anything, it's a good experience.

grammar.meaning: rather than ~, (it's more accurate to say) ~
grammar.formation: Plain form / な-adj stem / noun + というより (often followed by むしろ)

question: 料理{りょうり}ができる（　　）、卵焼{たまごや}きとサラダぐらいしか作{つく}れません。
full_sentence: 料理{りょうり}ができるといっても、卵焼{たまごや}きとサラダぐらいしか作{つく}れません。
translation: I say I can cook, but I can only make rolled omelets and salads.
explanation: 〜といっても means 'although I say ~ / even though it's called ~, (in reality it's less than you might think)'. The speaker first says 'I can cook' and then immediately limits that statement: only a rolled omelet and a salad. The structure 〜ぐらいしか〜ない 'only about ~' in the second half is the clue that the first statement is being toned down. Connection: plain form (verb / adjective) or noun + といっても (料理ができるといっても, 旅行といっても).
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜というより means 'rather than ~, it's more like ~' and replaces the first description with a more accurate one: 料理というより、ただ野菜を切っただけだ 'it's not so much cooking as just cutting vegetables'. Our sentence doesn't replace 'I can cook'; it limits it.

Wrong. 〜ばかりか means 'not only ~ but also ~' and adds something in the SAME direction: 彼は料理ができるばかりか、ケーキまで焼ける 'he not only can cook, he can even bake cakes'. Our second half says the skill is limited, which goes in the opposite direction.

Wrong. 〜からには means 'now that ~, since ~ (so I must / I will)' and is followed by a duty or resolution: 料理を習うからには、本格的な料理を作れるようになりたい 'since I'm learning to cook, I want to be able to make real dishes'. It cannot introduce a limitation.
Correct. できるといっても…しか作れません 'I say I can cook, but I can only make ~'. Plain form + といっても + a limitation.

vocab.example: お弁当{べんとう}に卵焼{たまごや}きを入{い}れた。
vocab.example_translation: I put a rolled omelet in the lunch box.

grammar.meaning: although I say ~, (it's not much / there is a limitation)

question: 薬{くすり}を飲{の}んだのに、風邪{かぜ}は治{なお}る（　　）、ますますひどくなった。
full_sentence: 薬{くすり}を飲{の}んだのに、風邪{かぜ}は治{なお}るどころか、ますますひどくなった。
translation: Even though I took medicine, far from getting better, my cold got even worse.
explanation: 〜どころか means 'far from ~, (actually the opposite)'. You deny the expected thing (getting better) and say that the reality is the complete opposite (it got worse). The words のに 'even though' and ますます 'more and more' show that things went in the opposite direction from what the medicine should have done. Connection: plain form of verbs and い-adjectives, な-adjective (stem or + な), or noun + どころか. どころか also has a second use, 'let alone': 漢字どころか、ひらがなも読めない 'he can't even read hiragana, let alone kanji'.
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜ばかりか means 'not only ~ but also ~' and adds a second fact in the SAME direction: 風邪が治ったばかりか、体も前より丈夫になった 'not only did my cold get better, my body also got stronger than before'. 'Not only getting better but also getting worse' is a contradiction.

Wrong. 〜ものの means 'although (it is true that) ~' and admits a fact before a contrast: 薬を飲んだものの、まだ熱が下がらない 'although I took medicine, my fever still hasn't gone down'. 治るものの would admit that the cold gets better, but it did NOT get better, so the sentence contradicts itself.
Correct. 治るどころか、ますますひどくなった 'far from getting better, it got even worse'. The reality is the opposite of the expectation.
Wrong. 〜につれて means 'as ~ (changes), ~ also changes' and links two gradual changes: 年を取るにつれて、体力が落ちる 'as you get older, your stamina drops'. 'As it got better, it got worse' is contradictory.

vocab.meaning: to get better, to be cured (illness, injury)
vocab.example: けがが治{なお}るまで、運動{うんどう}は休{やす}んでください。

vocab.example: 約束{やくそく}したのに、彼{かれ}は来{こ}なかった。

grammar.formation: Plain form / な-adj (stem or + な) / noun + どころか
grammar.example: 彼{かれ}は謝{あやま}るどころか、逆{ぎゃく}に怒{おこ}り出{だ}した。

grammar.example: 新{あたら}しいパソコンを買{か}ったものの、使{つか}い方{かた}がよくわからない。

grammar.example: 山{やま}を登{のぼ}るにつれて、気温{きおん}が下{さ}がってきた。

question: 来週{らいしゅう}は大事{だいじ}な試験{しけん}があるので、今{いま}は旅行{りょこう}（　　）。
full_sentence: 来週{らいしゅう}は大事{だいじ}な試験{しけん}があるので、今{いま}は旅行{りょこう}どころではない。
translation: I have an important exam next week, so now is no time for traveling.
explanation: 〜どころではない means 'this is no time for ~, I'm in no situation to ~'. It says that because of some pressing situation (here, an important exam next week), the speaker has no time, money, or mental room for something (traveling). The reason clause 〜ので 'because ~' is the clue: it explains why travel is out of the question right now. Connection: noun or verb dictionary form + どころではない (旅行どころではない, 遊んでいるどころではない). In casual speech you will also hear どころじゃない.
choice_notes: Correct. 旅行どころではない 'this is no time for travel'. The exam leaves no room for it. Noun + どころではない.

Wrong. 〜にほかならない means 'is nothing other than ~, is precisely ~' and gives a firm explanation or definition: 合格できたのは努力したからにほかならない 'I passed precisely because I worked hard'. 'Now is nothing other than travel' makes no sense here.
Wrong. 〜に違いない means 'must be ~, I'm sure ~' (a confident guess): 彼は今ごろ旅行中に違いない 'he must be on a trip right now'. It doesn't fit a sentence that rules out traveling because of an exam.

Wrong. 〜に限る means '~ is the best (thing to do)' and gives a recommendation: 疲れたときは温泉旅行に限る 'when you're tired, nothing beats a hot-spring trip'. Recommending travel contradicts the reason given (an important exam next week).

vocab.example: これは祖母{そぼ}からもらった大事{だいじ}な指輪{ゆびわ}だ。
vocab.example_translation: This is a precious ring I received from my grandmother.

vocab.example: 明日{あした}は数学{すうがく}の試験{しけん}がある。
vocab.example_translation: There's a math exam tomorrow.

vocab.example: 冬休{ふゆやす}みに北海道{ほっかいどう}を旅行{りょこう}した。
vocab.example_translation: I traveled around Hokkaido during the winter break.

grammar.meaning: this is no time for ~, (I'm) in no position to ~
grammar.formation: Noun / verb dictionary form + どころではない (casual: どころじゃない)
grammar.example: 仕事{しごと}が忙{いそが}しくて、休{やす}みどころではない。
grammar.example_translation: I'm so busy with work that a day off is out of the question.

grammar.meaning: is nothing other than ~, is precisely ~ (a firm explanation)
grammar.formation: Noun + にほかならない / plain form + から + にほかならない
grammar.example: 彼{かれ}が成功{せいこう}したのは、努力{どりょく}を続{つづ}けたからにほかならない。
grammar.example_translation: The reason he succeeded is nothing other than that he kept working hard.

grammar.meaning: must be ~, there's no doubt that ~ (a confident guess)
grammar.formation: Plain form / な-adj stem / noun + に違いない
grammar.example: 電気{でんき}が消{き}えているから、彼{かれ}はもう寝{ね}たに違{ちが}いない。
grammar.example_translation: The lights are off, so he must have gone to bed already.

grammar.meaning: ~ is the best (thing to do), nothing beats ~
grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / ない-form / noun + に限る
grammar.example: 暑{あつ}い日{ひ}は冷{つめ}たいビールに限{かぎ}る。
grammar.example_translation: On hot days, nothing beats a cold beer.

question: 実際{じっさい}に使{つか}ってみ（　　）、この機械{きかい}が本当{ほんとう}に便利{べんり}かどうかはわからない。
full_sentence: 実際{じっさい}に使{つか}ってみないことには、この機械{きかい}が本当{ほんとう}に便利{べんり}かどうかはわからない。
translation: Unless I actually try using it, I can't tell whether this machine is really convenient.
explanation: 〜ないことには means 'unless ~, (you can't / nothing will happen)' and is ALWAYS followed by a negative result such as わからない, できない, or 始まらない. It states that the first action is an absolutely necessary condition. The ending 〜かどうかはわからない 'can't tell whether ~' is the clue. Connection: verb ない-form + ことには (使ってみない + ことには); with adjectives: 安くないことには, 静かでないことには. Similar meanings: 〜なければ, 〜てからでないと.
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜ないうちに means 'before ~ (happens)' and is followed by an action you should take in time: 暗くならないうちに帰ろう 'let's go home before it gets dark'. わからない is not an action taken in time, so it doesn't fit.
Correct. 使ってみないことには…わからない 'unless I try using it, I can't tell'. ない-form + ことには + negative result.

Wrong. 〜ないことはない means 'it's not that ~ not; it is possible (but not certain)' and normally comes at the END of a clause, often followed by が or けど: 使えないことはないが、ちょっと不便だ 'it's not that I can't use it, but it's a bit inconvenient'. It cannot introduce a condition for the next clause like this.
Wrong. 〜ものの means 'although ~' and expresses a contrast. 'Although I don't try it, I can't tell' makes no sense. Correct use: 買ったものの、まだ一度も使っていない 'I bought it, but I haven't used it even once'.

vocab.example: 実際{じっさい}に行{い}ってみると、写真{しゃしん}よりきれいだった。
vocab.example_translation: When I actually went there, it was prettier than in the photos.

vocab.example: この機械{きかい}の使{つか}い方{かた}を教{おし}えてください。
vocab.example_translation: Please teach me how to use this machine.

vocab.example: 駅{えき}に近{ちか}くて便利{べんり}なアパートだ。
vocab.example_translation: It's a convenient apartment close to the station.

vocab.example: 明日{あした}晴{は}れるかどうか、わからない。

vocab.meaning: to try doing ~ (to see what it's like)
vocab.example: 新{あたら}しいレストランに行{い}ってみた。
vocab.example_translation: I tried going to a new restaurant.

grammar.meaning: unless ~, (nothing can happen / can't ~)
grammar.formation: Verb ない-form / い-adj 〜くない / な-adj, noun + でない + ことには + negative result
grammar.example: 本人{ほんにん}に聞{き}かないことには、本当{ほんとう}の理由{りゆう}はわからない。

grammar.meaning: before ~ (happens), while it is still not ~

grammar.example: 雨{あめ}が降{ふ}らないうちに、洗濯物{せんたくもの}を取{と}り込{こ}もう。

grammar.meaning: it's not that ~ not; ~ is possible (with some hesitation)
grammar.formation: Verb ない-form / い-adj 〜くない / な-adj 〜でない + ことはない
grammar.example: 辛{から}い料理{りょうり}も食{た}べられないことはないが、あまり好{す}きではない。
grammar.example_translation: It's not that I can't eat spicy food, but I don't really like it.

grammar.meaning: although ~ (it is true, but the result is not what the first half suggests)
grammar.formation: Plain form / な-adj + な (or である) / noun + である + ものの
grammar.example: 新{あたら}しいパソコンを買{か}ったものの、使{つか}い方{かた}がよくわからない。
grammar.example_translation: Although I bought a new computer, I don't really know how to use it.

question: A「明日{あした}までにこの資料{しりょう}、作{つく}れる？」B「うーん、徹夜{てつや}すれば作{つく}れない（　　）けど、ちょっと厳{きび}しいね。」
full_sentence: A「明日{あした}までにこの資料{しりょう}、作{つく}れる？」B「うーん、徹夜{てつや}すれば作{つく}れないことはないけど、ちょっと厳{きび}しいね。」
translation: A: 'Can you make these materials by tomorrow?' B: 'Hmm, it's not impossible if I stay up all night, but it's a bit tough.'
explanation: 〜ないことはない means 'it's not that ~ can't / doesn't; it IS possible, but...'. The double negative makes a hesitant, partial 'yes'. B means 'I could make it if I stayed up all night, but it would be hard'. The clues are the hesitation うーん and the following けど、ちょっと厳しいね, which show a weak, reluctant yes rather than a clear yes or a clear no. Connection: verb ない-form + ことはない (作れない + ことはない). Be careful: verb DICTIONARY form + ことはない is a different pattern meaning 'there's no need to ~' (心配することはない 'there's no need to worry').
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜ないことには means 'unless ~' and must be followed by a negative result in the same sentence: 資料がないことには、会議が始められない 'unless we have the materials, we can't start the meeting'. It cannot be followed directly by けど.
Wrong. 〜ないわけがない means 'there's no way ~ can't', which equals 'definitely can'. 作れないわけがない 'of course I can make it' is a strong yes, which clashes with the hesitant うーん and ちょっと厳しいね.
Correct. 作れないことはない 'it's not that I can't make it (I could)'. ない-form + ことはない, a reluctant 'it's possible'.

Wrong. 〜ものか expresses strong emotional denial or refusal: あんな店、二度と行くものか 'I'll never go to that shop again!'. With a negative, 〜ないものか means 'isn't there some way to ~?' (a wish): なんとか作れないものか 'isn't there some way I could make it?'. Neither meaning fits B's reluctant 'yes', and it can't be followed by けど here.

vocab.example_translation: Please make copies of the meeting materials in advance.

question: 新{あたら}しい事業{じぎょう}を始{はじ}める（　　）、社員{しゃいん}全員{ぜんいん}で目標{もくひょう}を確認{かくにん}した。
full_sentence: 新{あたら}しい事業{じぎょう}を始{はじ}めるにあたって、社員{しゃいん}全員{ぜんいん}で目標{もくひょう}を確認{かくにん}した。
translation: On starting the new business, all the employees confirmed the goals together.
explanation: 〜にあたって means 'when ~, on the occasion of ~' and is used for an important or special event, especially a new start (opening a business, entering a school, getting married, moving abroad). It is followed by what someone does in preparation for, or at, that occasion. Here: at the start of a new business, everyone confirms the goals. Connection: verb dictionary form or noun + にあたって (more formal: にあたり). A near-synonym is 〜に際して.
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜にかけては means 'when it comes to ~ (a skill), no one beats ~' and talks about someone's ability: 料理にかけては誰にも負けない 'when it comes to cooking, I'm second to none'. It attaches to nouns, not to a verb like 始める, and the meaning doesn't fit.

Wrong. 〜にしたがって means 'as ~ (changes), ~ (also changes)' or 'in accordance with ~': 事業が大きくなるにしたがって、社員も増えた 'as the business grew, the number of employees increased'. Confirming the goals once is not a gradual change.
Wrong. 〜を問わず means 'regardless of ~' and attaches to nouns such as 年齢, 男女, or 経験: 経験を問わず、誰でも応募できる 'anyone can apply, regardless of experience'. It cannot follow a verb like 始める.
Correct. 始めるにあたって 'on starting, when we start'. Dictionary form + にあたって for an important occasion.

question: この店{みせ}では、客{きゃく}の予算{よさん}（　　）料理{りょうり}の内容{ないよう}を変{か}えてくれる。
full_sentence: この店{みせ}では、客{きゃく}の予算{よさん}に応{おう}じて料理{りょうり}の内容{ないよう}を変{か}えてくれる。
translation: At this restaurant, they adjust the dishes according to the customer's budget.
explanation: 〜に応じて means 'according to ~, in response to ~, depending on ~' and shows that something changes to match a factor that varies (budget, age, ability, season, situation). Here, the content of the meal changes depending on how much each customer wants to spend. The verb 変える 'to change' is the clue: に応じて is typically followed by verbs of changing or adjusting (変える, 選ぶ, 決める, 調整する). Connection: noun + に応じて; before a noun it becomes に応じた (予算に応じた料理 'dishes that match the budget').
choice_notes: Correct. 予算に応じて 'according to the budget'. Noun + に応じて + a change that matches it.

Wrong. 〜をめぐって means 'over ~, concerning ~' and is followed by words of debate or conflict (議論する, 争う, 対立する): 予算をめぐって、会議で意見が分かれた 'opinions were divided at the meeting over the budget'. 変えてくれる is not a dispute.
Wrong. 〜に先立って means 'prior to ~, before ~' and attaches to an event: 開店に先立って、試食会が開かれた 'a tasting event was held before the opening'. A budget is not an event that happens at a point in time.
Wrong. 〜にわたって means 'over (a whole period or area), throughout ~' and attaches to time spans or ranges: 三日間にわたって会議が行われた 'the conference was held over three days'. A budget is not a period or an area.

grammar.formation: Noun (time span / area / number of times) + にわたって / にわたる + noun
grammar.example: 台風{たいふう}の影響{えいきょう}で、広{ひろ}い範囲{はんい}にわたって停電{ていでん}した。
grammar.example_translation: Because of the typhoon, there was a power outage over a wide area.

question: このイベントには、年齢{ねんれい}や経験{けいけん}（　　）、誰{だれ}でも参加{さんか}できます。
full_sentence: このイベントには、年齢{ねんれい}や経験{けいけん}にかかわらず、誰{だれ}でも参加{さんか}できます。
translation: Anyone can take part in this event, regardless of age or experience.
explanation: 〜にかかわらず means 'regardless of ~, no matter ~' and says that a difference (old or young, experienced or not) does not affect the result. 誰でも 'anyone' in the second half is the clue: if anyone can join, then age and experience make no difference. Connection: noun + にかかわらず. It usually follows nouns that contain a range or contrast (年齢 'age', 天候 'weather', 男女 'men and women', 経験の有無 'with or without experience') or a pair of opposites (行く行かないにかかわらず 'whether you go or not'). A near-synonym is 〜を問わず. Don't confuse it with にもかかわらず 'despite', which has the extra も.
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜に応じて means 'according to ~' and says that something CHANGES to match the factor: 年齢に応じて料金が変わる 'the fee changes depending on age'. 'Anyone can join according to age' contradicts 誰でも.
Correct. 年齢や経験にかかわらず 'regardless of age or experience'. Noun + にかかわらず: the differences don't matter.

Wrong. 〜にこたえて means 'in response to (a request or expectation)' and attaches to nouns like 期待, 要望, or 声: ファンの声にこたえて、追加公演が決まった 'in response to the fans' voices, extra concerts were scheduled'. Age and experience are not requests.

Wrong. 〜に限って means 'only (in this case), of all times / people' and singles out one case: 急いでいる時に限って、電車が遅れる 'the train is late precisely when I'm in a hurry'. Singling out one case contradicts 誰でも 'anyone'.

question: いつもは暇{ひま}なのに、デートの約束{やくそく}がある日{ひ}（　　）、急{きゅう}な仕事{しごと}が入{はい}ってしまう。
full_sentence: いつもは暇{ひま}なのに、デートの約束{やくそく}がある日{ひ}に限{かぎ}って、急{きゅう}な仕事{しごと}が入{はい}ってしまう。
translation: I'm usually free, but on the very days when I have a date planned, urgent work comes up.
explanation: 〜に限って means 'only on / in ~, of all times ~' and singles out one particular case in which something (usually bad or annoying) happens, against what normally happens. The contrast いつもは暇なのに 'I'm usually free, but...' and the regretful 〜てしまう tell you the speaker feels unlucky that work comes up exactly on date days. Connection: noun + に限って (日に限って, 時に限って). This 'bad luck' use often appears as 〜時に限って. Another use expresses trust: うちの子に限って、うそをつくはずがない 'MY child, of all children, would never lie'.
choice_notes: Wrong, though the form looks similar. 〜に限らず means 'not only ~ (but also others)': デートの日に限らず、毎日忙しい 'I'm busy every day, not only on date days'. That contradicts いつもは暇なのに 'I'm usually free'.
Wrong. 〜にかけては means 'when it comes to (a skill) ~' and praises an ability: 料理にかけては誰にも負けない. A day is not a skill.
Wrong. 〜に応じて 'according to ~' shows that something changes to match a factor: 季節に応じてメニューが変わる 'the menu changes according to the season'. 'Work comes up according to the date day' makes no sense.
Correct. 約束がある日に限って 'precisely on the days when I have plans'. Noun + に限って for an unlucky special case.

vocab.example: 暇{ひま}な時{とき}は何{なに}をしていますか。

vocab.example: 友達{ともだち}と三時{さんじ}に会{あ}う約束{やくそく}をした。

vocab.example: 週末{しゅうまつ}に仕事{しごと}が入{はい}ってしまった。

grammar.formation: Noun + にかけては

grammar.meaning: according to ~, in response to ~, depending on ~
grammar.formation: Noun + に応じて / noun + に応じた + noun
grammar.example: 年齢{ねんれい}に応{おう}じて、料金{りょうきん}が変{か}わる。
grammar.example_translation: The fee changes according to age.

question: 兄{あに}は勉強{べんきょう}は苦手{にがて}だが、料理{りょうり}（　　）、プロにも負{ま}けない。
full_sentence: 兄{あに}は勉強{べんきょう}は苦手{にがて}だが、料理{りょうり}にかけては、プロにも負{ま}けない。
translation: My older brother is bad at studying, but when it comes to cooking, he is as good as a professional.
explanation: 〜にかけては means 'when it comes to ~, in the field of ~' and is used to say that someone's ability in one area is excellent. It is almost always followed by praise such as 誰にも負けない 'second to none', 一番だ 'the best', or 自信がある 'confident'. The clue is プロにも負けない 'doesn't lose even to professionals', which describes a high level of skill. The contrast with 勉強は苦手だが 'he's bad at studying, but' also highlights one special area of talent. Connection: noun + にかけては (also にかけても).
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜にとっては means 'for ~, from the viewpoint of ~' and is used with a person or group who judges something: 兄にとって、料理は一番の楽しみだ 'for my brother, cooking is his greatest pleasure'. 料理 is not a person with a viewpoint.
Wrong. 〜にしては means 'for ~, considering ~' and the result differs from what you'd expect from that standard: 初心者にしては上手だ 'he's good for a beginner'. 'For cooking, he's as good as a pro' makes no sense.
Correct. 料理にかけては 'when it comes to cooking'. Noun + にかけては + praise of a skill.
Wrong. 〜に対しては means 'toward ~, against ~' (the target of an action or attitude): 兄は子どもに対しては優しい 'my brother is kind toward children'. It does not talk about skill in a field.

vocab.meaning: bad at, weak in; (something one) dislikes
vocab.example: 私{わたし}は数学{すうがく}が苦手{にがて}だ。
vocab.example_translation: I'm bad at math.

grammar.meaning: when it comes to ~ (an ability), (no one is better)
grammar.formation: Noun + にかけては (also にかけても)
grammar.example: 足{あし}の速{はや}さにかけては、彼{かれ}がクラスで一番{いちばん}だ。
grammar.example_translation: When it comes to running fast, he's the best in the class.

grammar.meaning: for ~, from the viewpoint of ~

grammar.example: 私{わたし}にとって、家族{かぞく}が一番{いちばん}大切{たいせつ}だ。
grammar.example_translation: For me, family is the most important thing.

grammar.meaning: for ~, considering ~ (the result differs from the expected standard)

grammar.example: 彼{かれ}は小学生{しょうがくせい}にしては、背{せ}が高{たか}い。

grammar.meaning: toward ~, against ~; in contrast to ~

question: あんなに毎日{まいにち}練習{れんしゅう}していたのだから、彼女{かのじょ}は合格{ごうかく}する（　　）。
full_sentence: あんなに毎日{まいにち}練習{れんしゅう}していたのだから、彼女{かのじょ}は合格{ごうかく}するに決{き}まっている。
translation: She practiced that hard every day, so of course she'll pass.
explanation: 〜に決まっている means 'it's certain that ~, of course ~' and shows the speaker's strong, almost subjective conviction. The reason clause 〜のだから 'since (as we all know) ~' gives the grounds, and the conclusion follows with confidence: hard daily practice → she will surely pass. Connection: plain form of verbs and い-adjectives, or な-adjective stem / noun + に決まっている (合格するに決まっている, 高いに決まっている, うそに決まっている). It is more conversational and emotional than 〜に違いない. The three wrong choices all express denial or refusal, the opposite of the logical conclusion.
choice_notes: Correct. 合格するに決まっている 'she's sure to pass'. Plain form + に決まっている for strong conviction.

Wrong. 〜わけがない means 'there's no way ~' (a strong denial): 全然練習しなかったのだから、合格するわけがない 'he didn't practice at all, so there's no way he'll pass'. After 'she practiced hard every day', denying that she'll pass makes no sense.
Wrong. 〜どころではない means 'this is no time for ~': 忙しくて旅行どころではない 'I'm too busy to even think about travel'. 'She's in no position to pass' makes no sense.

Wrong. 〜ものか means 'as if ~! / never!' (a strong emotional denial): あんな人に負けるものか 'as if I'd lose to someone like that!'. 合格するものか 'as if she'd pass!' is the opposite of the conclusion that hard practice leads to.

question: ファンの強{つよ}い要望{ようぼう}（　　）、そのバンドは追加{ついか}公演{こうえん}を行{おこな}うことを決{き}めた。
full_sentence: ファンの強{つよ}い要望{ようぼう}にこたえて、そのバンドは追加{ついか}公演{こうえん}を行{おこな}うことを決{き}めた。
translation: In response to strong demand from fans, the band decided to hold additional concerts.
explanation: 〜にこたえて means 'in response to ~, to meet / live up to ~' and is used with nouns that express what people want from you: 要望 'request', 期待 'expectation', 声 'voices', ニーズ 'needs'. The fans strongly wanted more, so the band responded by adding concerts. The noun 要望 'request, demand' is the clue. Connection: noun + にこたえて (in kanji: に応えて); before a noun: にこたえる (要望にこたえる商品 'a product that meets demand').
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜をめぐって means 'over ~, concerning ~' and is followed by debate or conflict: 公演の中止をめぐって、ファンの間で議論が起きた 'a debate broke out among fans over the canceled concert'. The band's decision is a response, not a dispute.
Correct. 要望にこたえて 'in response to the request'. Noun (request / expectation) + にこたえて.
Wrong. 〜にわたって means 'over (a period or area)': 三か月にわたって全国でツアーを行った 'they toured the country over a period of three months'. A request is not a time span or an area.
Wrong. 〜に代わって means 'in place of ~, on behalf of ~': 病気の歌手に代わって、別の歌手が歌った 'another singer sang in place of the sick singer'. The band did not act in place of a request.

question: 新製品{しんせいひん}の発売{はつばい}（　　）、記者{きしゃ}向{む}けの説明会{せつめいかい}が開{ひら}かれた。
full_sentence: 新製品{しんせいひん}の発売{はつばい}に先立{さきだ}って、記者{きしゃ}向{む}けの説明会{せつめいかい}が開{ひら}かれた。
translation: Prior to the release of the new product, a briefing for reporters was held.
explanation: 〜に先立って means 'prior to ~, before ~' and is used when something is done as preparation before an important event (a release, an opening, a match, a ceremony). It is formal and very common in news and business Japanese. Here the press briefing happened before the product went on sale. The event noun 発売 'release' is the clue. Connection: noun or verb dictionary form + に先立って (formal written style: に先立ち). Similar: 〜に先がけて, or simply 〜の前に.
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜に沿って means 'along ~' or 'in line with (a plan, policy, or wishes)': 川に沿って歩く 'walk along the river', 計画に沿って進める 'proceed according to the plan'. A release is a one-time event, not something you follow along.
Wrong. 〜にかけては means 'when it comes to (a skill)': 歌にかけては誰にも負けない 'when it comes to singing, I'm second to none'. It does not express time order.
Correct. 発売に先立って 'prior to the release'. Noun (an event) + に先立って.

Wrong. 〜に反して means 'contrary to ~' and attaches to nouns like 予想 'prediction', 期待 'expectation', or 規則 'rules': 予想に反して、新製品はあまり売れなかった 'contrary to expectations, the new product didn't sell well'. 'Contrary to the release, a briefing was held' makes no sense.

question: 彼{かれ}は日本{にほん}に来{き}てまだ半年{はんとし}（　　）、日本語{にほんご}がずいぶん上手{じょうず}だ。
full_sentence: 彼{かれ}は日本{にほん}に来{き}てまだ半年{はんとし}にしては、日本語{にほんご}がずいぶん上手{じょうず}だ。
translation: For someone who came to Japan only six months ago, his Japanese is quite good.
explanation: 〜にしては means 'for ~, considering ~' and says that the result is different from what you would expect based on the first fact. Only half a year in Japan → you would expect basic Japanese → but his Japanese is quite good. The word まだ 'only, still' stresses how short the time is, which sets up the surprise. Connection: noun or plain form + にしては (半年にしては, 初めてにしては, 子どもにしては). It is used for a judgment about a specific person or thing, often with surprise, mild praise, or mild criticism. It is close to 〜わりに, but にしては usually takes a specific value or status (半年, 子ども, 初めて, この値段), while わりに can also take a general scale word on its own (年齢のわりに, 値段のわりに).
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜だけあって means 'as you'd expect from ~' and links a cause to a result that MATCHES it: 十年も住んでいただけあって、日本語が上手だ 'as you'd expect from someone who lived there ten years, his Japanese is good'. Only half a year is not a reason to expect good Japanese, so the cause and result don't match.

Wrong. 〜からといって means 'just because ~ (it doesn't mean ~)' and must be followed by a negative such as 〜とは限らない or 〜わけではない: 半年住んだからといって、日本語が話せるとは限らない 'just because you lived there six months doesn't mean you can speak Japanese'. Our sentence ends positively (上手だ). Also, after a noun you need だ: 半年だからといって.
Wrong. 〜どころか means 'far from ~, (actually the opposite)': 上手どころか、あいさつもできない 'far from being good, he can't even say hello'. 'Far from half a year, his Japanese is good' makes no sense.
Correct. まだ半年にしては 'for (only) half a year'. Noun + にしては + a result different from expectation.

question: 新入社員{しんにゅうしゃいん}の皆{みな}さんは、このマニュアル（　　）作業{さぎょう}を進{すす}めてください。
full_sentence: 新入社員{しんにゅうしゃいん}の皆{みな}さんは、このマニュアルに沿{そ}って作業{さぎょう}を進{すす}めてください。
translation: New employees, please carry out your work following this manual.
explanation: 〜に沿って has two related meanings: (1) 'along ~' for something long such as a river or a road (川に沿って歩く), and (2) 'in line with ~, following ~' for a plan, a policy, a manual, or someone's wishes. Here it is meaning (2): do the work following the steps written in the manual. The noun マニュアル 'manual' is the clue, since a manual is something you follow. Connection: noun + に沿って; before a noun: に沿った (マニュアルに沿った作業 'work that follows the manual'). Near-synonyms: 〜にしたがって, 〜に基づいて.
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜に先立って means 'prior to ~' and attaches to an event: 作業に先立って、マニュアルを読んでください 'please read the manual before starting the work'. A manual is not an event.
Correct. マニュアルに沿って 'following the manual'. Noun + に沿って.
Wrong. 〜にかけては means 'when it comes to (a skill)': パソコンにかけては彼が一番だ 'when it comes to computers, he's the best'. It cannot tell someone how to do their work.
Wrong. 〜に代わって means 'in place of ~, instead of ~': 休んだ田中さんに代わって、私が作業を進めた 'I carried on the work in place of Tanaka, who was absent'. Working 'in place of the manual' makes no sense.

question: 本日{ほんじつ}は店内{てんない}改装{かいそう}工事{こうじ}（　　）、休業{きゅうぎょう}いたします。
full_sentence: 本日{ほんじつ}は店内{てんない}改装{かいそう}工事{こうじ}につき、休業{きゅうぎょう}いたします。
translation: Due to interior renovation work, we are closed today.
explanation: 〜につき has two uses. Here it means 'due to ~, because of ~' and is a formal expression used on notices, signs, and announcements (休業 'closed', 工事中 'under construction', 禁煙 'no smoking', etc.). The clue is the formal, notice-style language: 本日 'today (formal)' and the humble verb いたします. Connection: noun + につき (often 〜中につき: 工事中につき, 会議中につき). The other use is 'per ~': 一人につき二枚まで 'up to two per person'.
choice_notes: Correct. 改装工事につき 'due to renovation work'. Noun + につき for a formal reason on a notice.
Wrong. 〜にとって means 'for ~, from the viewpoint of ~' and is used with a person or group: 客にとって、急な休業は不便だ 'for customers, a sudden closure is inconvenient'. Construction work has no viewpoint.

Wrong. 〜にかけて means 'from ~ to ~, through ~' and covers a range of time or place, usually in the form AからBにかけて: 今夜から明日にかけて雨が降る 'it will rain from tonight through tomorrow'. It does not express a reason.

Wrong (it looks similar to につき!). 〜につれて means 'as ~ (changes), ~ (also changes)': 工事が進むにつれて、店がきれいになっていった 'as the work progressed, the shop became more and more beautiful'. It needs two gradual changes and does not express a reason.

question: 年{とし}を取{と}る（　　）、昔{むかし}のことをよく思{おも}い出{だ}すようになった。
full_sentence: 年{とし}を取{と}るにつれて、昔{むかし}のことをよく思{おも}い出{だ}すようになった。
translation: As I've gotten older, I've come to recall the old days more often.
explanation: 〜につれて means 'as ~ (changes), ~ (also changes)' and links two gradual changes that move together. 年を取る 'to grow older' is a gradual change, and 〜ようになった 'came to (do)' shows a gradual change in the result. When both halves describe a change over time, think につれて (or its near-synonyms 〜にしたがって, 〜とともに, 〜に伴って). Connection: verb dictionary form, or a noun that implies change (時代の変化につれて 'as the times change'), + につれて. All three wrong choices mark ONE point in time (an occasion), not a gradual process.
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜にあたって means 'on the occasion of ~' for a one-time, important event: 引っ越しにあたって、荷物を整理した 'I sorted out my belongings in preparation for the move'. Getting older is a continuous process, not one occasion.

Wrong. 〜に際して means 'at the time of ~, on the occasion of ~' (formal, for a specific event): 入学に際して、書類を提出する 'submit the documents upon entering the school'. Like にあたって, it marks one point in time, not a gradual change.
Correct. 年を取るにつれて 'as I get older'. Dictionary form + につれて + a gradual change (ようになった).
Wrong. 〜に先立って means 'prior to ~' (before an event): 出発に先立って、説明会が開かれた 'a briefing was held before departure'. 'Before getting older, I came to recall the past' makes no sense.

vocab.example: 祖母{そぼ}は年{とし}を取{と}っても元気{げんき}だ。
vocab.example_translation: My grandmother is still healthy even though she has gotten old.

vocab.example: 昔{むかし}、この町{まち}には大{おお}きな川{かわ}があった。
vocab.example_translation: Long ago, there was a big river in this town.

grammar.formation: Verb dictionary form / noun (of change) + につれて
grammar.example: 山{やま}を登{のぼ}るにつれて、気温{きおん}が下{さ}がってきた。

question: 今回{こんかい}の優勝{ゆうしょう}は決{けっ}して偶然{ぐうぜん}ではない。選手{せんしゅ}たちの厳{きび}しい練習{れんしゅう}の成果{せいか}（　　）。
choices: に越{こ}したことはない
full_sentence: 今回{こんかい}の優勝{ゆうしょう}は決{けっ}して偶然{ぐうぜん}ではない。選手{せんしゅ}たちの厳{きび}しい練習{れんしゅう}の成果{せいか}にほかならない。
translation: This championship win is by no means a coincidence. It is nothing other than the result of the players' hard training.
explanation: 〜にほかならない means 'is nothing other than ~, is precisely ~' and gives a firm, confident explanation of what something really is or why it happened. The first sentence rejects one explanation (it's not luck), and the second sentence states the true one (hard training). This 'not A - it's nothing but B' structure is a typical setting for にほかならない. Connection: noun + にほかならない; for reasons, plain form + から + にほかならない (努力したからにほかならない). It is formal and used in writing and speeches. Two wrong choices (に限る, に越したことはない) give advice about what is best to do, which cannot explain a past result.
choice_notes: Wrong. 〜に限る means '~ is the best (thing to do)' and gives a recommendation: 疲れたときは寝るに限る 'when you're tired, sleeping is the best thing'. 'The result of training is the best thing to do' is not a recommendation and doesn't explain the win.
Wrong. 〜どころではない means 'this is no time for ~': 試合の前で、遊ぶどころではない 'it's right before the match, so this is no time to play around'. It doesn't fit an explanation of why they won.
Wrong. 〜に越したことはない means 'it's best to ~, nothing is better than ~' (common-sense advice): 練習は多いに越したことはない 'the more practice, the better'. Like に限る, it is advice, not an explanation of a past result.
Correct. 成果にほかならない 'is nothing other than the result'. Noun + にほかならない for a firm explanation.

vocab.example: 私{わたし}たちのチームが大会{たいかい}で優勝{ゆうしょう}した。
vocab.example_translation: Our team won the tournament.

grammar.meaning: is nothing other than ~, is precisely ~ (a firm explanation)

grammar.example: 彼{かれ}が成功{せいこう}したのは、努力{どりょく}を続{つづ}けたからにほかならない。

grammar.example_translation: I'm so busy with work that a day off is out of the question.

grammar.meaning: it's best to ~, nothing is better than ~ (common-sense advice)

grammar.example: 健康{けんこう}のためには、早{はや}く寝{ね}るに越{こ}したことはない。
grammar.example_translation: For your health, it's best to go to bed early.

question: 激{はげ}しい雨{あめ}（　　）、試合{しあい}は予定{よてい}どおり行{おこな}われた。
full_sentence: 激{はげ}しい雨{あめ}にもかかわらず、試合{しあい}は予定{よてい}どおり行{おこな}われた。
translation: Despite the heavy rain, the match was held as scheduled.
explanation: 〜にもかかわらず means 'despite ~, even though ~' and introduces a result that goes against what you would expect from a specific fact. Heavy rain → you would expect the match to be canceled → but it was held as planned. Connection: noun + にもかかわらず (激しい雨にもかかわらず), or plain form + にもかかわらず (雨が降っているにもかかわらず; な-adjectives and nouns can use である: 危険であるにもかかわらず). It is a formal version of 〜のに. Watch out: the one-character difference も changes the meaning completely. にかかわらず (without も) means 'regardless of' and is used with a range of possibilities, not with one fact that actually happened.
choice_notes: Wrong (the classic trap). 〜にかかわらず means 'regardless of ~' and attaches to a noun that contains a range of possibilities (天気, 年齢, 有無) or to a pair of opposites: 天気にかかわらず試合を行う 'we'll hold the match whatever the weather'. 激しい雨 is one specific fact that actually happened, not a range of possibilities, so it needs にもかかわらず 'despite'.
Correct. 激しい雨にもかかわらず 'despite the heavy rain'. Noun + にもかかわらず + an unexpected result.
Wrong. 〜のみならず means 'not only ~ (but also)' (formal): 雨のみならず、風も強かった 'not only was there rain, but the wind was also strong'. It adds information in the same direction; it doesn't mean 'despite'.

Wrong. 〜をきっかけに means 'with ~ as the trigger, (something started)': 雨宿りをきっかけに、二人は話すようになった 'sheltering from the rain together was how the two of them started talking'. Holding the match as planned is not something the rain triggered.

vocab.example: 夜{よる}になって、風{かぜ}が激{はげ}しくなった。
vocab.example_translation: At night, the wind became fierce.

vocab.example: 日曜日{にちようび}にテニスの試合{しあい}がある。

vocab.meaning: to hold, to carry out, to conduct (formal)

grammar.formation: Noun / plain form (な-adj, noun + である) + にもかかわらず

grammar.example_translation: He came to work despite having a fever.

grammar.example: 天気{てんき}にかかわらず、試合{しあい}は行{おこな}われる。

grammar.example: この問題{もんだい}は日本{にほん}のみならず、世界中{せかいじゅう}で起{お}きている。
grammar.example_translation: This problem is happening not only in Japan but all over the world.

grammar.formation: Noun / plain form + の + をきっかけに
grammar.example: 留学{りゅうがく}をきっかけに、料理{りょうり}を始{はじ}めた。
grammar.example_translation: Studying abroad was what got me started cooking.

question: 工事{こうじ}のため、この道路{どうろ}は来月{らいげつ}から三{さん}か月{げつ}（　　）通行止{つうこうど}めになる。
full_sentence: 工事{こうじ}のため、この道路{どうろ}は来月{らいげつ}から三{さん}か月{げつ}にわたって通行止{つうこうど}めになる。
translation: Because of construction work, this road will be closed to traffic for three months starting next month.
explanation: 〜にわたって means 'over (the whole of) ~, throughout ~' and emphasizes that something continues across a long period or a wide area. 三か月 'three months' is a length of time, which is the clue. It sounds more formal and emphatic than simply 三か月間. Connection: noun of time span, distance, area, or number of times + にわたって (三日間にわたって, 全国にわたって, 十回にわたって); before a noun: にわたる (三か月にわたる工事 'construction lasting three months').
choice_notes: Correct. 三か月にわたって 'over a period of three months'. Time span + にわたって.

Wrong. 〜にかけて means 'from ~ to ~' and needs a starting point and an end point, usually as AからBにかけて with two points in time or place: 来月から再来月にかけて 'from next month through the month after'. 三か月 is a length, not an end point.
Wrong. 〜につき means 'per ~' or 'due to ~ (on formal notices)': 一人につき千円 '1,000 yen per person'. '(Closed) per three months' doesn't make sense.
Wrong. 〜をめぐって means 'over ~ (an issue)' and is followed by debate or conflict: 工事をめぐって、住民が反対している 'residents are protesting over the construction'. A length of time is not an issue to argue about.

vocab.example: 雪{ゆき}で道路{どうろ}が凍{こお}っている。
vocab.example_translation: The road is frozen because of the snow.

vocab.example: 事故{じこ}のため、高速道路{こうそくどうろ}が通行止{つうこうど}めになった。

vocab.example: 家{いえ}の前{まえ}で道路{どうろ}工事{こうじ}をしている。

vocab.example: 大雪{おおゆき}のため、電車{でんしゃ}が止{と}まった。
vocab.example_translation: The trains stopped because of heavy snow.

vocab.meaning: ~ months (counter for a number of months)
